notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported comparisons are from the benchmark's interactive challenges.

name: REAL: Benchmarking Autonomous Agents on Deterministic Simulations of Real Websites
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). All evaluated interactions occur in controlled simulations of websites.
summary: Introduces REAL, a benchmark of deterministic website replicas with 112 tasks covering information retrieval and state-changing browser actions.

name: RedTeamCUA: Realistic Adversarial Testing of Computer-Use Agents in Hybrid Web-OS Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: RedTeamCUA combines a virtual-machine OS environment with containerized websites for controlled prompt-injection tests spanning both interfaces. Its RTC-Bench contains 864 examples and can initialize agents at injection points to separate attack susceptibility from navigation failures.

name: MCPWorld: A Unified Benchmarking Testbed for API, GUI, and Hybrid Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. The platform or GUI evaluation setting was additionally checked in the primary full text.
summary: MCPWorld evaluates API, GUI, and hybrid computer-use agents with 201 tasks in applications whose source can be instrumented and extended with MCP support. It verifies completion from application behavior and packages the testbed in containers with GPU support.

name: Measuring Harmfulness of Computer-Using Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). The misuse tasks are evaluated in a sandbox.
summary: Introduces CUAHarm, 104 computer-use misuse tasks in a sandbox with verifiable rewards, and studies whether language models can monitor unsafe agent actions.

name: WebMall -- A Multi-Shop Benchmark for Evaluating Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: WebMall provides four simulated online shops with heterogeneous product data for comparison shopping, related-product searches, and checkout tasks. It evaluates web agents with different observation formats and memory configurations in a fixed offline environment.

name: UI-TARS-2 Technical Report: Advancing GUI Agent with Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: UI-TARS-2 combines scalable trajectory generation, stabilized multi-turn reinforcement learning, and a sandbox that supports GUI, filesystem, and terminal actions. The report evaluates the resulting agent across web, desktop, Android, and game tasks and analyzes training stability.

name: Orcust: Stepwise-Feedback Reinforcement Learning for GUI Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Orcust combines principle-constrained reward modeling with GUI trajectory collection in instrumented virtual machines. Environment-checkable and model-derived principles guide stepwise feedback for grounding, basic operations, and complete task execution.

name: UISim: An Interactive Image-Based UI Simulator for Dynamic Mobile Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Planning for agent navigation is described as a potential application of the simulator.
summary: Introduces UISim, an image-based mobile UI simulator that predicts the next screen layout after an action and renders the resulting screen for testing and data generation.

name: Efficient Multi-turn RL for GUI Agents via Decoupled Training and Adaptive Data Curation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: DART separates GUI reinforcement learning into asynchronous environment, rollout, data-management, and training services. It curates experience by task difficulty, successful trajectories, and step uncertainty while correcting rollout-policy mismatch, with evaluation on OSWorld.

name: SCUBA: Salesforce Computer Use Benchmark
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: SCUBA evaluates enterprise UI navigation and CRM workflows with 300 task instances derived from Salesforce user interviews. Salesforce sandbox execution and milestone-based assessment support comparisons between zero-shot agents and agents given demonstrations.

name: Your Harness is Not Secure: Benchmarking Real-world Threat of Command Line Interface Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3).
summary: Introduces AdvCLI, a sandbox benchmark for evaluating whether command-line agents carry out security-relevant operating-system tasks across multiple hosts.

name: WARC-Bench: Web Archive Based Benchmark for GUI Subtask Executions
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: WARC-Bench packages dynamic web pages as replayable archives and evaluates short navigation subtasks involving components such as date pickers and scrollable containers. It also studies supervised training followed by reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards on these browser interactions.

name: WEBSERV: A Full-Stack and RL-Ready Web Environment for Training Web Agents at Scale
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: WebServ combines copy-on-write container environments with a compact DOM-derived browser interface for training web agents. Network-aware waiting supports action execution in single-page applications, with evaluations and reinforcement-learning experiments on WebArena-Lite.

name: GhostEI-Bench: Do Mobile Agents Resilience to Environmental Injection in Dynamic On-Device Environments?
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). The attacks are evaluated within Android emulators.
summary: Introduces GhostEI-Bench, a benchmark that injects deceptive UI events into Android emulator workflows to assess mobile agents and analyze failures from actions and screenshots.

name: OSGym: Scalable OS Infra for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: OSGym supplies full operating-system sandboxes with GUIs for parallel computer-use data collection and training. It combines per-replica state management, hardware-aware orchestration, copy-on-write virtual-machine disks, and layered failure recovery.

name: ceLLMate: Sandboxing Browser AI Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: ceLLMate constrains browser-agent authority through an extension that applies policies at the HTTP layer. It evaluates this sandbox against prompt-injection attacks in WASP, avoiding dependence on brittle low-level click and keystroke policies.

name: InfiniteWeb: Scalable Web Environment Synthesis for GUI Agent Training
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: InfiniteWeb generates functional, interconnected websites and task evaluators using shared specifications and task-driven development. It evaluates website construction and the transfer of GUI policies trained in these synthetic web environments to OSWorld and Online-Mind2Web.

name: EvoCUA: Evolving Computer Use Agents via Learning from Scalable Synthetic Experience
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: EvoCUA combines task synthesis with executable validators, asynchronous sandbox rollouts and iterative policy updates. It turns successful routines and analyzed failures into supervision and evaluates the evolving agent on OSWorld.

name: Computer Environments Elicit General Agentic Intelligence in LLMs
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3).
summary: LLM-in-Sandbox gives agents a minimal computer environment for resource access, file management and code execution; LLM-in-Sandbox-RL trains models to use it.

name: Blind Gods and Broken Screens: Architecting a Secure, Intent-Centric Mobile Agent Operating System
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). The reported comparison with a screen-based mobile assistant uses MobileSafetyBench.
summary: Analyzes security risks in screen-based mobile agents and proposes Aura, an agent runtime with structured interactions, app-agent isolation and mediated communication.

name: GUI-GENESIS: Automated Synthesis of Efficient Environments with Verifiable Rewards for GUI Agent Post-Training
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: GUI-GENESIS reconstructs applications as lightweight web environments with executable assertions for reward computation. It evaluates the cost of these training environments and transfer from synthetic interaction training to held-out real tasks.

name: AutoWebWorld: Synthesizing Infinite Verifiable Web Environments via Finite State Machines
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: AutoWebWorld turns finite-state task models into interactive websites whose actions and goal states can be checked programmatically. It generates verified trajectories for training and evaluates transfer to WebVoyager and Online-Mind2Web.

name: Safe and Scalable Web Agent Learning via Recreated Websites
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. The abstract promises a release upon acceptance; this annotation does not verify artifact availability.
summary: Introduces VeriEnv, which recreates websites as executable training environments and exposes internal state through a Python SDK for task generation and deterministic reward checks. Experiments examine web-agent learning across new and expanded site environments.

name: Gym-Anything: Turn any Software into an Agent Environment
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces Gym-Anything, where a setup agent configures software environments and an independent auditor checks the resulting evidence. CUA-World supplies long-horizon tasks across professional applications, with experiments on trajectory distillation and test-time auditing.

name: KnowU-Bench: Towards Interactive, Proactive, and Personalized Mobile Agent Evaluation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces KnowU-Bench, an Android emulator benchmark for mobile agents that evaluates preference elicitation, proactive decisions, consent and GUI task execution.

name: AcademiClaw: When Students Set Challenges for AI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: AcademiClaw benchmarks OpenClaw agents on long academic workflows, scoring task completion in isolated Docker sandboxes with rubrics and a safety audit.

name: Constraining Host-Level Abuse in Self-Hosted Computer-Use Agents via TEE-Backed Isolation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: A TEE-backed design confines host operations by self-hosted computer-use agents, classifying and authorizing actions before constrained local execution.

name: Weblica: Scalable and Reproducible Training Environments for Visual Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces Weblica, which combines HTTP-level capture and replay with website-grounded environment synthesis. The resulting interactive web environments support reinforcement learning and tests of navigation transfer and inference-time scaling.

name: Computer Use at the Edge of the Statistical Precipice
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). DigiWorld comprises 15 sandboxed mobile applications.
summary: DigiWorld is a sandboxed mobile-app benchmark for computer-use agents, paired with PRISM environment principles and a confidence-interval aggregation method.

name: WildClawBench: A Benchmark for Real-World, Long-Horizon Agent Evaluation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: WildClawBench evaluates CLI agents on long, multimodal tasks in Docker containers with real tools, using task checks, side-effect audits, and a semantic judge.

name: Orchard: An Open-Source Agentic Modeling Framework
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). The computer-use agent is one of three recipes in a broader agentic modeling framework.
summary: Orchard provides an environment service and training recipes for several agent domains, including Orchard-GUI, a vision-language computer-use agent.

name: ShopGym: An Integrated Framework for Realistic Simulation and Scalable Benchmarking of E-Commerce Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Its agent evaluation uses generated tasks in sandbox shops.
summary: ShopGym builds sandbox e-commerce storefronts from live shops and generates catalog-grounded tasks for evaluating web shopping agents in resettable environments.

name: TClone: Low-Latency Forking of Live GUI Environments for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: TClone versions live GUI workspaces through snapshots, isolated forks, rollback and selective commit or merge. It separates fast branch creation from durable checkpoints using copy-on-write sharing, filesystem versioning and asynchronous checkpointing, with end-to-end agent-loop latency measurements.

name: ScaleWoB: Guiding GUI Agents with Coding Agents via Large-Scale Environmental Synthesis
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Mobile, desktop and automotive interfaces are simulated as webpages; this does not assert native deployment on those platforms.
summary: Introduces ScaleWoB, which synthesizes interactive GUI environments as backend-free webpages with verifiable rewards. Its mobile-oriented benchmark evaluates agent execution and compares selected synthetic tasks with real-app behavior.

name: CUA-Gym: Scaling Verifiable Training Environments and Tasks for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. The abstract promises future open sourcing; this annotation does not independently verify artifact release or licensing.
summary: Presents CUA-Gym, which co-generates instructions, initial and target states, and executable reward checks through generator-discriminator iterations. Mock web applications expand training environments, with learned agents evaluated on OSWorld-Verified and WebArena.

name: MobileGym: A Verifiable and Highly Parallel Simulation Platform for Mobile GUI Agent Research
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. The simulator is browser-hosted; the abstract does not identify a native mobile operating system.
summary: Introduces MobileGym, a browser-hosted simulation of mobile app interactions whose configurable JSON state supports deterministic judging and parallel rollouts. MobileGym-Bench adds parameterized tasks, with experiments examining online training and transfer to real devices.

name: PhoneWorld: From Real-App Trajectories to Dynamic and Verifiable Environments for Phone-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces PhoneWorld, which converts observed app pages, transitions and state changes into executable Android environments through a build-inspect-repair process. Generated tasks and programmatic verifiers support benchmarking, trajectory collection and online training.

name: OpenWebRL: Demystifying Online Multi-turn Reinforcement Learning for Visual Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The abstract reports results on Online-Mind2Web and DeepShop.
summary: Introduces OpenWebRL, a framework for training visual web agents with online multi-turn reinforcement learning on live websites, including browser infrastructure and success judging.

name: AOHP: An Open-Source OS-Level Agent Harness for Personalized, Efficient and Secure Interaction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported task-completion, token-cost, and security-policy results come from preliminary experiments.
summary: Introduces AOHP, an Android OS-level harness that treats agents as system actors and provides adaptive interfaces, agent interfaces, and information-flow controls.

name: Untrusted Content Masking for Web Agents with Security Guarantees
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Untrusted Content Masking uses DOM structure to redact untrusted webpage regions before agent observation. A sandboxed interaction interface separates privileges so browser actions can proceed under the proposed trust-boundary model without exposing protected content to the planner.

name: UniClawBench: A Universal Benchmark for Proactive Agents on Real-World Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces UniClawBench, a benchmark of proactive agents on bilingual real-world tasks, evaluated in live Docker containers with stepwise checkpoints and simulated user feedback.

name: EvoCUA-1.5: Online Reinforcement Learning for Multi-turn Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: EvoCUA-1.5 trains multi-turn desktop agents through online reinforcement learning in executable sandboxes. It combines step-level policy optimization, task filtering and calibration, an adaptive curriculum, and asynchronous rollout handling with staleness control.

name: OpenForgeRL: Train Harness-native Agents in Any Environment
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: OpenForgeRL connects stateful agent harnesses to reinforcement-learning infrastructure through a model-call recording proxy and isolated rollout containers. Its validation includes browser and computer-use agents, alongside tool-oriented agents, and examines how harness choice affects learned reliability.

name: Echoverse: Deep, Evolving Environments for Training Computer-Use Agents at Scale
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces Echoverse, which compiles specifications into stateful applications with database-grounded graders and uses rollouts to improve both the environments and agent policies. It examines behavioral depth, targeted interface practice, and environment repair as sources of training value.

name: Invisible Ink Threats: Adversarial Goals Behind Legitimate Tasks in Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). HITLCUA simulates human participation through an API-simulated user.
summary: Introduces II-Bench for low-harm indirect prompt injections against computer-use agents and HITLCUA for testing them in virtual-machine and web environments with simulated user review.

name: Training Needs Trustworthy Worlds: Verified Synthetic Web Environments for Agent Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Builds synthetic websites with verified navigation, backend state, and feasible tasks to provide reliable supervision for web-agent training.

name: Spine-Branch Coordination for Multi-agent Computer Use
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported experiments use 200 Odysseys tasks and three CUA backbones.
summary: Introduces Spine-Branch Coordination, which assigns a main task flow to one virtual-machine state and uses parallel branch machines to gather information for computer-use agents.

name: BrowserForge: Scaling Web Episode via Parallel Browser Sandboxes
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces BrowserForge, which combines broad website sourcing, parallel browser sandboxes, and task-proposer/solver interaction to collect verified web trajectories. The pipeline uses page structure during synthesis but trains a policy that acts from screenshots.

name: CUA-Universe: A Scalable and Dynamic Environment for Hybrid GUI+CLI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Turns desktop applications into reproducible GUI-and-CLI environments and generates verified hybrid trajectories for agent post-training.

name: APPSim-Bench: Bridging Real-world Apps and Reproducible Evaluation for Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces controlled simulated mobile apps with deterministic backend data and outcome checks for reproducible evaluation of realistic interactions.

name: CoArena: Evaluating Computer-Use and Multi-Agent Systems in Real Time
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The five-system example uses 211 illustrative votes.
summary: Introduces CoArena, an evaluation method where user tasks run concurrently in sandboxed desktops and blind pairwise judgments update a public leaderboard.

name: RiskChainBench: A Benchmark for Obfuscated Platform Message Restoration and Evidence-Grounded Web Investigation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The web investigations use corresponding local web environments.
summary: Introduces RiskChainBench, pairing obfuscated-message restoration with web-agent investigation of linked sites in labeled local web environments.

name: CUA-Sandbox: Efficient Environments for Computer-Use Agent Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces CUA-Sandbox, which separates each rollout’s mutable state from shared initialized software runtimes. State-scoped execution and transactional resets or branches aim to reduce training-environment costs while retaining original interfaces and evaluators.

name: StateFork: Branchable Infrastructure for Agent Exploration
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The work studies terminal sessions that modify files, processes, shell context, and local services.
summary: Introduces StateFork and Waypoint for branching and restoring terminal-agent sessions so agents can explore multiple paths while preserving execution state.

name: SoftwareGym: Scaling Computer-Use Agent Training with Diverse Synthesized Software Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces SoftwareGym, a pipeline that synthesizes runnable GUI applications and iteratively repairs them using execution checks. It also provides a task benchmark and studies whether training on synthesized application trajectories transfers to other computer-use environments.

name: MAI-Gym: An Open All-in-One Platform for GUI Agent Evaluation and RL Training across Mobile and Computer Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Unifies GUI evaluation, trajectory collection, environment synthesis, and online reinforcement learning across mobile, computer, and web tasks.

name: BlenderWorld: Benchmarking Visual Agents for 3D Creation from Real-World References
notes: The evaluated agents use Linux shell/Python/MCP tools and can inspect viewport screenshots; graphical CUA control and Windows/macOS are future work. Each agent is run once per task, with different Codex/Claude Code harnesses across systems. Scores combine weighted rubric satisfaction and model-rated visual quality. Tool counts include unsuccessful calls and do not establish matched compute or successful actions.
summary: Benchmarks agents creating editable Blender projects through shell, Python and MCP tools, judging delivered scenes with multi-view renders, task-specific rubrics and visual-quality ratings.

name: CUA-Lite: An Open Platform for Computer Use Agents
notes: Reviewed the complete official abstract and selected v1 methods, training and limitations sections. WebVoyager uses offline mirrors; VM-free sandboxes are Linux-only, and reported desktop/mobile gains do not establish unseen-app transfer.
summary: CUA-Lite unifies environment interfaces, supervised data formats and per-model harnesses for evaluation, reinforcement learning and supervised fine-tuning across desktop, browser and mobile tasks.

name: Agent World Model in the Wild: Computer-Use Agent Environment Synthesis
notes: Reviewed the complete abstract and selected v1 synthesis, training and evaluation sections. The system uses hybrid GUI/MCP/CLI interfaces. Evaluation includes benchmark subsets and model-based judgments, so reported scores are not treated as directly comparable GUI-only results.
summary: WildAWM synthesizes resettable GUI/MCP/CLI environments and cross-interface tasks, using execution-based checks of solvability, difficulty and verifier consistency before supervised and reinforcement learning.

name: WebAnything: From the Wild Web to Scalable Agent Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Reconstruction uses browser-observable material collected after initial setup and authorization.
summary: Introduces WebAnything, a framework that reconstructs reusable, resettable website environments from real URLs for web-agent training and evaluation.

name: WebHarbor: Docking Real Websites for Evolving GUI Agent Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The environments reconstruct real websites under deterministic control.
summary: Introduces WebHarbor, a suite of 153 executable website environments and 3,518 tasks for evaluating and training GUI web agents on interactive workflows.

notes: Recorded as adjacent: the publisher presents Firecrawl as a web data API for AI agents, and its search, scrape, map and crawl endpoints return page content as Markdown, HTML, JSON or screenshots without operating the page. Interact continues from a scrape result: POST /v2/scrape/{scrapeId}/interact takes either a natural-language prompt, which it carries out by clicking, typing and scrolling, or Playwright code, and returns a CDP URL and live-view URLs; named profiles keep browser state such as logins between sessions. The Browser Sandbox (POST /v2/interact) opens a standalone isolated browser session with Playwright and the agent-browser CLI preinstalled, CDP access and an embeddable interactive live view. The /agent endpoint gathers data from a prompt by searching and navigating sites and runs on the publisher's Spark 2 model. The homepage HTML changes on every request, so the primary receipt is the documentation introduction. The homepage also links the repository github.com/firecrawl/firecrawl; which hosted features that code includes was not reviewed, and its license does not cover the hosted service. Pricing, availability and reliability were not independently tested, and no task was run.
summary: Hosted web data API for AI agents that searches and scrapes pages into Markdown or JSON, with an Interact endpoint and browser sandbox in which prompts or Playwright code click, type and fill forms.

name: OSWorld VirtualBox Ubuntu image
notes: Adjacent: an environment image that the curated OSWorld benchmark boots when run with VirtualBox, not a benchmark or training set by itself. At revision c4e80049 the repository holds only Ubuntu.zip (12,395,902,743 bytes) and .gitattributes; there is no dataset card, so it names no paper and declares no license, and every license slot stays unknown. At OSWorld commit b138d348 the VirtualBox provider downloads this archive on x86 hosts, extracts it and imports Ubuntu/Ubuntu.ovf from the extracted files with VBoxManage, supports only Ubuntu tasks, and refuses macOS hosts. The name is editorial, taken from that provider. The image was not downloaded or booted.
summary: Hub host of the Ubuntu virtual machine archive that OSWorld's VirtualBox provider downloads on x86 hosts and imports with VBoxManage; the repository has no card or license declaration.

name: Wuying Agentic Mobile
notes: The overview describes MobileUseAgent, an Android agent built for Wuying Cloud Phone that parses the native Android control tree, joined to the OpenClaw agent framework, with Qwen models for screen perception and instruction understanding; it also lists social-app engagement that imitates human behavior to avoid platform risk controls as a use case. The quick-start page, reached from the discovered URL whose cloud-phone-mobileclaw slug now redirects to cloud-phone-jvs-mobile, calls the service a public beta sold as monthly node plans with credits for model use, and sends tasks to the OpenClaw agent from a chat page. The X-PLUG/MobileAgent README announces Mobile-Agent-v3.5 on Wuying Cloud Phone and links that page; the Alibaba Cloud pages do not name Mobile-Agent-v3.5. Receipts use the Markdown exports of the help pages because their HTML embeds a per-request tracking ID.
summary: Alibaba Cloud Wuying service that runs Qwen-driven agents (MobileUseAgent with OpenClaw) in cloud Android containers to carry out natural-language tasks across apps, for process automation and app testing.

summary: A cloud agent platform that gives agents persistent computers with browser, GUI, terminal, and file access, alongside project workspaces and workflow triggers.

name: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
notes: A general agent hosting platform, so the scope is adjacent. Its computer-interaction component is AgentCore Browser: a containerized browser reached through a WebSocket automation endpoint (usable from Strands, Nova Act or Playwright) and a live-view endpoint where a person can watch the session and interact with it directly. Sessions default to 15 minutes and last at most 8 hours. Session recording, available for custom browsers, stores DOM changes, user actions, console logs and network events in the customer's S3 bucket. Amazon Nova Act (url:dec156cbf0cb1181f7b6) is cataloged separately. The landing URL redirects to its trailing-slash form over plain HTTP, so evidence is read from the HTTPS trailing-slash address. Availability and pricing were not independently tested.
summary: AWS managed agent platform whose Browser tool runs isolated cloud browser sessions with automation and live-view streams and optional recording, alongside runtime, memory, gateway and code-execution services.

name: OpenMobile-2 extended Android AVDs
notes: The Hub dataset repository at revision 4d2be380 has no card and no license declaration. It lists 143 files, about 130 GB by listed sizes: seven AVD directories (MineAndroid plus auto, general-user, manual, senior, student and travel variants), their .ini pointers and install_avd.sh. Every config.ini targets android-33 with arm64-v8a on a Pixel 6 profile and Play Store disabled. The script requires an Apple Silicon Mac, installs the android-33 Google APIs arm64-v8a system image through sdkmanager, and warns that -wipe-data erases the installed apps. Which apps each variant holds is not documented, and the images were not downloaded or booted. The OpenMobile2-Code README links this repository as 'Extended Android AVDs' in its release list; that repository's Apache-2.0 license does not cover these images or the Android system image.
summary: Seven preconfigured Pixel 6 emulator images for Android API 33 (arm64) with an Apple Silicon install script, listed in the OpenMobile-2 release as its extended Android AVDs.
